title: ChemMiner: A Large Language Model Agent System for Chemical Literature Data Mining
claim_supported: automated candidate extraction can be much faster and cheaper than manual collection
study_design: expert benchmark plus manual-versus-agent cost and speed comparison
key_result: manual precision 90.05% at 288 seconds and USD 1.41 per reaction versus agent precision 87.45% at 0.43 seconds and USD 0.0025
limitation: cost excludes negative-evidence adjudication licensing normalization and maintenance

title: ReactionSeek: LLM-powered literature data mining and knowledge discovery in organic synthesis
claim_supported: a low-custom-code pipeline can scale to an archival collection
study_design: multi-modal extraction over Organic Syntheses with benchmark evaluation
key_result: reports over 95% precision and recall for key parameters and produces a large structured dataset
limitation: does not publish a full per-record economic accounting and focuses on positive reported procedures

title: ChemDataExtractor: A Toolkit for Automated Extraction of Chemical Information from the Scientific Literature
claim_supported: open tooling can reduce repeated implementation cost
key_result: MIT-licensed toolkit achieved useful F-scores across several extraction tasks
limitation: rule maintenance and domain adaptation costs are not quantified

title: Application of Large Language Models in Chemistry Reaction Data Extraction and Cleaning
claim_supported: prompting fine-tuning and verification offer multiple cost-quality operating points
study_design: comparison of GPT and Llama-family workflows
key_result: GPT-4 prompt tuning performed best while smaller fine-tuned models could follow schemas with hundreds of examples
limitation: no complete labor licensing and maintenance cost model

title: Negative chemical data boosts language models in reaction outcome prediction
claim_supported: negative data can create value when positive experiments are scarce
study_design: controlled and realistic HTE datasets with reaction prediction
key_result: reports strong performance using as few as 20 positives when supported by at least 40 times more negatives
limitation: benefit depends on access to large well-characterized negative sets; collection cost not reported
